title: Installing a Toilet Below Grade with a Macerator (This Old House)
summary: This Old House demonstrates installing a toilet below grade using a macerator unit integrated with a lavatory drain. The video contrasts a standard siphon-jet toilet with a P-trap-like discharge design that pushes waste through a small 3/4-inch line to the house drainage, aided by a macerator grinder and an automatic sensor. It covers routing the discharge up a wall to a vent stack, priming and cementing PVC joints, and securing the unit to the subfloor without a traditional closet flange using brass lag screws. The demonstration also shows connecting the porcelain outlet to the macerator with a rubber gasket and stainless clamps, tying in the lav drain to the reservoir, venting, and finishing with a water-supply hookup and test.
topics: reservoir with macerator grinder and sensor

sections.title: Macerator toilet vs siphon jet and key components
sections.description: The presenter distinguishes a macerator-based toilet from a traditional siphon-jet toilet, noting that this unit discharges through the back via a small 3/4 inch line and uses a reservoir with a grinder and sensor to pump waste.

sections.title: Discharge routing, lav drain tie-in, and vent planning
concepts: potential vertical reach (up to 16 ft) and distance (up to 150 ft)
sections.description: The discharge is routed up the wall toward a vent stack. The plan includes priming and cementing PVC joints, connecting the lav drain into the macerator reservoir, and tying the vent into the house drainage system.

sections.title: Securing a toilet without a traditional flange
sections.description: With no floor flange, the toilet is secured using brass lag screws driven into the subfloor. The installer marks, pre-drills, and precisely positions the unit to prevent movement.

sections.title: Connecting toilet to macerator: gasket and clamps
sections.description: The porcelain outlet is connected to the macerator using a rubber accordion gasket, tightened with stainless steel clamps, and an adapter supplied by the manufacturer is installed.

sections.title: Water supply hookup and system test
sections.description: The water supply is reconnected, the tank is filled, and a final check confirms the system is ready.
